scope: Completed ESMC GFP smoke run evidence audit; no inference, environment modification, or result regeneration was performed.

mask_id_audit.runtime_resolution: runner instantiates EsmcTokenizer and selects tokenizer.mask_token_id before model.config.mask_token_id

official_tokenizer_source.evidence: SEQUENCE_VOCAB documents | as 31 and <mask> as 32, calls this the canonical vocabulary used by all ESMC checkpoints, and says indices are hard-coded into model weights

mask_id_audit.conclusion: config.json mask_token_id=31 is stale/inconsistent serialized metadata for this interface; it did not control the actual masked input in this run. Cross-implementation numerical parity remains a separate pending comparison.

resolved.attention: pre-LN fused QKV; Q/K LayerNorm across full d_model=2560 before 40x64 head reshape; RoPE; SDPA in this run

bias_audit.wording_boundary: Do not generalize linear bias=False into an assertion that every LayerNorm in the implementation lacks a bias parameter.

scoring.conditional_preference_definition: masked-LM log p(observed amino acid) minus log p(best alternative among the 20 standard amino acids)
scoring.interpretation: After clipping, 210 negative margins share a zero constraint component; their rank differences are driven by novelty, while the 28 positive margins retain a nonzero constraint component.

representation_normalization.scope: each input representation independently along its final d_model axis
representation_normalization.formula: x = (x - mean(x, dim=-1, keepdim=True)) / (std(x, dim=-1, keepdim=True) + 1e-5)

1.description_summary: Detector of accessible peptide chain termini—primarily the extreme N-terminus (initiator methionine and immediate neighbors) in flexible, unstructured tails; position-specific rather than residue-specific—with occasional weak recognition of the C-terminus; common but not universal.

Initiator methionine at the very start of the polypeptide chain (M1), i.e., the translation start residue, independent of protein family, taxonomy, membrane association, or presence of signal/leader/propeptide regions; often annotated as post-translationally removed and typically situated in a flexible, coil-like N-terminus.

20.description_summary: Residue-level detector for small side chains (primarily Gly and Ala, occasionally Ser/Thr) at beta-strand positions, with a strong propensity for the repeating strand sites of right-handed parallel beta-helix (PbH1) solenoids common in carbohydrate-active, surface/secreted proteins; the same preference also appears in beta-sheets of diverse soluble enzyme folds, indicating a structural rather than catalytic motif.

24.description_summary: Residue-level detection of β-strand-connecting loop/turn positions (β-hairpin/coil apex residues) across diverse β-sheet–rich domains, with a strong preference for Gly and Asx (Asp/Asn) and occasional His/Thr at the turn.

Glycine‑centered tight β‑turn/hairpin loop motif at sheet–sheet or coil‑to‑β transitions, typically an Asx/Ser/Thr–Gly sequence (often D–G, sometimes P/S/T preceding and Lys nearby), marking short, well‑ordered loops that link adjacent β‑strands across diverse folds

26.description_summary: Short, solvent-exposed loop/turn motifs (beta-turn/hinge segments) used as binding or catalytic micro-sites across many folds; typically proline- and charge/hydrophobe-rich SLiMs rather than a family-specific signature, hence frequent in extracellular/repeat-rich proteins but present broadly in soluble enzymes and regulators

40.description_summary: Residues at beta-strand starts and edge strands (loop-to–beta-strand junctions) in non‑transmembrane regions; the feature marks short stretches within beta-sheets and immediately preceding coils, consistent with generic beta-structure preferences rather than a specific function

Beta-strand–connecting loop/turn residues (beta-hairpin/strand–strand linkers) in beta-sheet–rich domains, often enriched for Gly and acidic residues; a generic structural motif rather than a function-specific signal

45.description_summary: Beta-strand secondary-structure signal: the feature marks residues within ordered β-sheets (DSSP class E), often in extracellular/luminal domains but broadly across taxa and functions; enrichment for polar/charged side chains within strands rather than specific catalytic motifs

91.description_summary: A general secondary-structure signal for short beta-strands and their flanking turns/coil in non-transmembrane regions (extracellular or cytosolic), with a preference for small/flexible or polar/charged residues; strongly depleted in alpha-helices, especially membrane-spanning helices.

173.description_summary: Acidic/polar residues in short coil/turn loops that connect beta-strands within repeat-based beta-sheet scaffolds—most prominently the surface loops of WD40 beta-propeller blades and MORN repeats; the feature flags periodic Asp/Glu/Asn/Ser/Thr positions in these inter-strand loops, with occasional weaker hits to analogous loops in unrelated enzymes.

174.description_summary: Beta-strand–connecting loop/turn residues (beta-hairpin/strand–strand linkers) in beta-sheet–rich domains, often enriched for Gly and acidic residues; a generic structural motif rather than a function-specific signal

195.description_summary: Generic detector of leucine side chains in alpha-helical contexts (including transmembrane and soluble helices), with occasional weaker responses to other hydrophobics; largely indifferent to specific functional motifs or protein class.

Intrinsic-disorder/low-complexity coil detector: marks residues in intrinsically disordered regions (low pLDDT, coil/flexible segments), with a bias toward proline-associated positions (often the residue immediately preceding Pro, e.g., S/T-P), commonly in terminal tails and flexible linkers across diverse proteins.

65.description_summary: Generic serine detector: the feature marks serine residues, with weaker affinity for threonine (and occasionally proline), and is especially prominent in low-complexity S/T-rich stretches; it is context- and structure-agnostic and does not correspond to a specific functional motif.

66.description_summary: Sequence-level detector for tyrosine residue identity (aromatic Tyr recognition), largely context-independent but with frequent emphasis on tyrosines positioned near Cys/His in C2H2-type zinc-finger motifs; weak cross-reactivity to other aromatics (Phe/Trp) and occasional neighboring acidic/amide residues.

67.description_summary: Residue-identity detector for glycine (G), with a mild bias toward intrinsically disordered/low-complexity segments (often including very N-terminal residues); pan-taxonomic and function-agnostic, but activation is sparse and frequently absent, becoming detectable mainly in glycine-rich low-complexity contexts; occasional weak responses to other small/polar residues.

sae.activation_interpretation_boundary: Raw activations are sparse feature magnitudes. They support feature lookup; values across distinct feature IDs are not a calibrated cross-feature confidence scale.
